data.hypothesis: A prior explicit-shuffle warp-first candidate was valid and faster than the baseline in repeated full-program measurements, but those measurements do not prove the block-local tree is the bottleneck. This contrasting experiment replaces its warp shuffle stages with the SM80+ native integer warp reduction, retaining a shuffle fallback, to test whether warp-reduction instruction cost matters while keeping the 128-thread tile and recursive launch structure unchanged. Unsigned modulo-2^32 intermediates plus an in-range final conversion preserve correctness when the exact final sum fits int32.

memory_lessons.applicability: This reduction candidate family and supplied benchmark cases; the observed comparison is full-program and does not isolate a kernel-level cause.
memory_lessons.claim: The explicit-shuffle warp-first candidate was correct on 10 supplied cases and measured a 30.295 μs mean across three samples, versus 46.244 μs for the baseline. This motivates testing a distinct warp reduction implementation, but does not establish why the full-program time changed.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the native-warp-reduction variant with the same correctness and repeated full-program protocol; compare it against the explicit-shuffle candidate and baseline.

data.notes: The valid prior candidate's three full-program samples were 30.767, 30.076, and 30.040 μs (mean 30.295 μs); the baseline samples were 46.565, 46.081, and 46.086 μs (mean 46.244 μs). The prior candidate passed all 10 supplied cases (n=1, 127, 1024, 65536, and 4194304, two seeds each), with guards intact and input unchanged. The memory record for 908efebec59a4521-h01 reports build failure or candidate timeout but gives no detailed diagnostic. This new proposal has no correctness or timing result yet; controller evaluation is required. Context reports GH200/CUDA 12.6.3; the native intrinsic is architecture-guarded and older architectures use the shuffle fallback.
transformations: Replaced explicit warp-shuffle reduction with __reduce_add_sync for SM80+ and retained the shuffle fallback for lower architectures; applied this warp-first reduction both to input values and the cross-warp combine.

Used unsigned 32-bit modular arithmetic for all partial sums and an explicit in-range conversion when storing the resulting bit pattern as int, avoiding signed intermediate overflow when the final exact sum fits int32.

Retained the 128-thread tile, zero-filled tail handling, four warp partials, recursive host stages, scratch-bank offsets, ABI, and default-stream ordering; set output to zero asynchronously for n <= 0.
